answer: Memory-hard sequential proofs requires every identity to maintain a RAM-bound verifiable delay function computed per identity. A sybil attacker must pay 2 dedicated RAM modules per clone, so a 1,000-clone farm needs 2,000 separate allocations. The protocol applies this via spot-checked delay-function outputs every epoch. The basalt ledger locks enrollment, the orchard verification step logs every proof, and the hollow bond vault settles penalt...
